title: Epoch lease expiry gating causes warmup suppression and tenant-serving starvation
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Summary: Several enterprise customers experienced sustained degraded throughput and frequent cold-starts during multi-region bursts over the weekend. Root cause analysis indicates an interaction between epoch-based lease expiry in the reserved-pool allocator and the warmup gating logic: when a tenant's lease was reissued precisely at epoch boundary the warmup credit recorder suppressed warmup signals for up to the next epoch window, preventing tenants from being admitted into warm pools even though burst headroom existed. This led to silent starvation for quiet-but-bursting tenants and violated burst SLAs.

Impact: Affected customers saw increased 95th/99th percentile latency and token queuing; several raised high-severity support tickets and one customer (FinHealth) initiated a formal escalation citing customer-facing outages. The condition was intermittent and correlated with epoch-aligned lease churn and small-tenant weightings.

Repro steps:
1) Configure a reserved pool with short epoch lease (30s) and conservative warmup credits.
2) Create a low-rps tenant with sudden burst load hitting the burst limit.
3) Force lease rotation on the allocator at epoch boundary while sending burst traffic.
4) Observe that warmup credit recorder flags the tenant as "suppress-warmup" for the remainder of the epoch window, preventing admission to warm pool nodes.

Root cause: The warmup gating state machine relied on "lease_renewal_timestamp" semantics that are not monotonic across raft leader transitions and epoch rollovers. A race between lease reissue and headroom recalculation led to the warmup sentinel being set with an expiry epoch that overshot the intended window. The autoscaler heuristics then deprioritized the tenant until an explicit recalculation or scale event occurred.

Mitigation applied (hotfix):
- Rollout small patch to allocator (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/allocator/pull/1287) that makes warmup gating use monotonic event IDs instead of epoch timestamps and clamps suppression to a configurable max_duration (default 10s).
- Emergency canary deployed to canary zone (us-west-2a) at 2026-03-12 03:14 UTC; monitored headroom and admission metrics.
- Temporarily increased warmup admission window for affected tenants via console override (internal toggle) to unblock customer traffic.

Observability / telemetry added:
- New metric allocator.warmup_suppression_count (tagged by tenant, pool, AZ).
- Alerting rule added: warmup_suppression_count > 5 for 2m triggers P1 pager.
- Dashboard: "Dedicated Autoscale Warmup Health" (Grafana) with heatmap of suppression by epoch and tenant. Link: https://grafana.internal.redwood/app/d/WarmupHealth/dedicated-warmup

Rollout plan:
- Complete automated test coverage in allocator unit + integration suite (tests added in PR).
- Gradual rollout across regions: canary (us-west-2a) -> us-east-1 -> eu-west-1 over 48 hours, with 1-hour observation window after each region.
- Post-rollout: revert console override and validate per-tenant SLA metrics.

Communication:
- Notified all impacted customers with interim mitigation and ETA for hotfix deployment. Customer comms template used: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1CustCommsWarmup (internal).
- Support runbook updated with quick-unblock steps and a pointer to telemetry dashboard.

Next steps / open work:
- Finish full rollout and verify regression dashboards (owner: Ravi Patel).
- Add chaos test that exercises epoch boundary lease renewal under load (owner: Sienna Morales).
- Review long-term autoscaler strategy to avoid epoch-aligned backpressure (proposal in PRD: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AutoscalePRD).
- Postmortem to be published (owner: Avery Chen) within 72 hours of full rollout completion.
